questions.text: A data scientist is developing a machine learning model that works on images and must make predictions in real-time. What type of inferencing should the data scientist implement?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Real-time inferencing

Real-time inferencing refers to the process of making immediate predictions on input data as it is received. In scenarios where decisions must be made instantly, such as image recognition for autonomous driving or facial recognition at security checkpoints, real-time inferencing is essential. The model processes input data and delivers predictions within milliseconds, ensuring the application functions seamlessly in real-world, time-sensitive conditions. Real-time inferencing is powered by highly optimized computational systems, such as GPUs, that can process large volumes of data rapidly. AWS services like Amazon SageMaker support real-time inferencing by deploying models in a low-latency environment, enabling instant predictions. This type of inferencing is ideal for machine learning tasks where the output must be generated immediately upon receiving the input, as in the case of the data scientist's requirement to work on image data and make predictions in real-time.

Incorrect

Batch inferencing

Batch inferencing processes multiple data inputs at once, making predictions on a collection of data, typically in non-time-sensitive scenarios. This option is less suited for real-time requirements since it does not handle individual requests immediately.

Delayed inferencing

Delayed inferencing is not a common industry term, but it implies making predictions after a certain delay, which contradicts the need for immediate or real-time decision-making. This approach is unsuitable for real-time systems where latency is critical.

Predictive inferencing

Predictive inferencing is a general term referring to using a trained model to make predictions. It doesn't specifically imply whether the predictions are made in real-time or in batches.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-deploy-models-realtime.html

questions.text: You need a foundation model that supports multiple modalities such as text, image, and audio. What criterion should guide your decision when selecting the pre-trained model?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Modality support

Modality support refers to a model's ability to handle different types of data such as text, images, and audio. In scenarios where you need a foundation model that can work with multiple types of inputs (e.g., text, image, and audio), prioritizing modality support is essential. Models that support multiple modalities are versatile and capable of processing and understanding a wide variety of data formats. This flexibility is crucial when building applications that require a combination of text, visual, and auditory inputs and outputs, such as multimedia content analysis or interactive AI systems.

Incorrect

Model size

While model size can affect performance, it does not address the need for handling multiple data types. Larger models might be more powerful but not necessarily better at supporting different modalities.

Cost of customization

Customization cost is important but secondary when the primary need is for a model that can handle multiple modalities. Ensuring the model supports different types of data is the first priority.

Input/output length

The ability to handle long inputs and outputs is important for specific tasks but is not directly related to the requirement of supporting multiple modalities.

questions.text: A business needs to create a voice-based chatbot to improve customer interaction. They need a service that can convert text to speech and recognize spoken words to create a conversational agent. Which AWS services should they choose for this purpose?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Polly and Amazon Lex

Amazon Lex is a service designed to build conversational interfaces like chatbots. It can recognize spoken words and interpret user intent using natural language understanding (NLU). Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that converts text responses generated by the chatbot into lifelike speech, allowing for interactive voice-based communication. By combining Amazon Lex (for understanding spoken input) and Amazon Polly (for converting text to speech), a business can create a fully functional voice-based chatbot to improve customer interaction.

Incorrect

Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Lex

Amazon Rekognition is used for image and video analysis, not voice processing. Amazon Lex is appropriate, but Rekognition does not fit the voice-based chatbot use case.

Amazon S3 and Amazon Transcribe

Amazon S3 is for data storage, and Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text but does not handle the chatbot functionality or text-to-speech conversion needed for a voice-based chatbot.

Amazon Kendra and Amazon Textract

Amazon Kendra is an enterprise search service, and Amazon Textract extracts text from documents. Neither is designed for creating conversational agents or voice interactions.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lex/latest/dg/what-is.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/what-is.html

questions.text: You are designing an AI-powered knowledge base application that leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). What is the primary advantage of using RAG in such applications?

options.text: RAG increases model training speed significantly.
RAG allows for integrating external knowledge sources to provide more accurate and context-aware responses.
RAG generates completely new responses without any pre-existing data.
RAG is suitable for models that require minimal fine-tuning.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

RAG allows for integrating external knowledge sources to provide more accurate and context-aware responses.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a powerful technique that combines the strengths of both retrieval-based and generation-based models. The key advantage of RAG is its ability to integrate external knowledge sources (like databases, documents, or the web) with generative models. This allows the system to generate more accurate, relevant, and context-aware responses by first retrieving the most relevant pieces of information and then using this data to generate a response. RAG is especially useful in scenarios where a vast amount of knowledge is needed or when the information changes frequently, ensuring the model‘s responses are up-to-date and reliable.

Incorrect

RAG generates completely new responses without any pre-existing data.

RAG doesn‘t generate completely new responses from scratch. It relies on retrieving external data to assist in generating responses, making them more grounded in real-world information.

RAG increases model training speed significantly.

RAG focuses on improving the quality of generated responses by incorporating retrieved data, but it doesn‘t directly impact model training speed.

RAG is suitable for models that require minimal fine-tuning.

While RAG can be used with pre-trained models, its main strength lies in enhancing responses with external data, not in reducing the need for fine-tuning.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/retrieval-augmented-generation

questions.text: You are developing a multilingual chatbot using a foundation model and need to support multiple languages. Which of the following criteria is most critical when selecting the pre-trained model for this application?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Multilingual support

Multilingual support refers to the model's capability to understand, process, and generate responses in multiple languages. When developing a multilingual chatbot, it is crucial to choose a model that supports a wide range of languages. This ensures that the chatbot can interact with users from different linguistic backgrounds seamlessly. Multilingual models, like those based on transformers (e.g., BERT, GPT), are pre-trained on diverse datasets across many languages, allowing the chatbot to switch between languages effortlessly. Additionally, good multilingual support minimizes the need for developing separate models for each language, saving time and resources. Selecting a model without proper multilingual abilities could result in poor user experiences and require significant additional work to support all the languages needed for the chatbot.

Incorrect

Cost of the model

While cost is always a factor in AI applications, it is not the primary consideration when multilingual support is required. A cheaper model may not offer robust multilingual capabilities.

Latency of inference

Latency is important but not the most critical factor when focusing on multilingual support. A faster model without language flexibility will not fulfill the application‘s main requirement.

Model complexity

Model complexity refers to how sophisticated the underlying architecture is. While it affects performance, it‘s less relevant than multilingual capability for this use case.

questions.text: A developer is tasked with building a chatbot that can respond to user inquiries and assist them in navigating the company's services. The solution needs to understand and respond to natural language inputs effectively. Which AWS service should the developer choose to implement this solution?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Lex

Amazon Lex is a fully managed service that allows developers to build conversational interfaces using voice and text. It powers the creation of sophisticated, natural language models that can be integrated into chatbots or voice assistants. Built on the same deep learning technologies as Amazon Alexa, Lex enables highly scalable and interactive AI-driven applications. It provides automatic speech recognition (ASR) to convert speech to text, and natural language understanding (NLU) to comprehend the intent behind the input. With easy integration into AWS services and real-time analytics, Lex is ideal for creating applications like virtual assistants, customer support bots, and interactive voice response systems.

Incorrect

Amazon Translate

Amazon Translate is a language translation service that converts text from one language to another. While useful for multilingual applications, it does not have the capabilities needed for building conversational interfaces.

Amazon Personalize

Amazon Personalize is a machine learning service that provides personalized recommendations based on user behavior. It's designed for recommendation engines and is not suited for creating chatbots.

Amazon Kendra

Amazon Kendra is an enterprise search service that uses machine learning to return more relevant search results across documents and databases. It does not handle conversational interfaces or natural language dialogues like Amazon Lex.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lex/latest/dg/what-is.html

questions.text: A company builds an AI model to classify emails as spam or non-spam. However, the model often misclassifies valid emails as spam, leading to important messages being lost. What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The model is overfitting to the training data, leading to poor performance on new emails.
The model has low variance and therefore does not misclassify emails frequently.
The model is biased toward labeling emails as non-spam.
The training dataset contains mostly spam emails, causing the model to misclassify non-spam emails.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

The training dataset contains mostly spam emails, causing the model to misclassify non-spam emails.

The most likely cause of the model misclassifying valid emails as spam is an imbalance in the training dataset. If the dataset contains mostly spam emails, the model becomes biased toward labeling emails as spam, which increases the likelihood of classifying valid, non-spam emails incorrectly. This type of imbalance makes it harder for the model to learn the correct distinctions between spam and non-spam, leading to more false positives. To resolve this issue, the dataset should be balanced, containing an equal or representative number of both spam and non-spam emails.

Incorrect

The model is biased toward labeling emails as non-spam.

This option suggests that the model labels more emails as non-spam, but in this case, the problem is the oppositevalid emails are being classified as spam, so the bias is toward spam, not non-spam.

The model is overfitting to the training data, leading to poor performance on new emails.

Overfitting refers to the model learning too much from the training data, including noise, leading to poor generalization on new data. However, the issue here is more likely due to dataset imbalance than overfitting.

The model has low variance and therefore does not misclassify emails frequently.

Low variance indicates that the model performs consistently across different data, but the issue here is not about consistency but the model‘s tendency to misclassify important emails as spam, likely due to biased training data.

questions.text: A company wants to build a recommendation engine that generates personalized content suggestions for its users. The company is considering using a generative AI model to achieve this goal. Which AWS service should they use to easily build, train, and deploy this generative AI model?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Personalize

Amazon Personalize is a machine learning service designed to build real-time personalized recommendations for users. It allows companies to easily build, train, and deploy recommendation engines without needing extensive machine learning expertise. Amazon Personalize can analyze user behavior, product metadata, and other data to provide personalized content suggestions. It's highly effective for use cases like recommending videos, articles, or products based on user preferences. This service automatically manages the entire machine learning workflow, from training models to deployment.

Incorrect

Amazon Polly

Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that converts written text into lifelike speech. It is not used for building recommendation engines or generating personalized content.

Amazon Translate

Amazon Translate is a service for translating text from one language to another. It is not designed for creating recommendation systems or analyzing user behavior.

AWS Glue

AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service used for preparing and loading data for analytics. While useful for data preparation, it is not intended for building recommendation engines or training generative AI models.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/personalize/latest/dg/what-is-personalize.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/personalize/latest/dg/personalize-with-gen-ai.html

questions.text: You are designing a prompt for a large language model to generate customer support responses. Which prompt engineering technique helps ensure that the model avoids certain types of responses or content?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Negative prompting

Negative prompting is a technique where you explicitly tell the AI model what content or responses to avoid. By specifying undesired topics, phrases, or behaviors, you guide the model away from generating certain types of content. This is especially useful in customer support settings to prevent the AI from producing inappropriate, offensive, or irrelevant responses. By incorporating negative prompts, you ensure that the AI‘s outputs align with company policies and provide a better experience for users by avoiding potential misunderstandings or issues.

Incorrect

Instruction prompting

Instruction prompting involves giving the AI specific directions on what you want it to do, focusing on desired actions rather than prohibiting certain content.

Contextual prompting

Contextual prompting provides the AI with background information or context to generate more relevant responses but doesn‘t specifically instruct it to avoid certain types of content.

Zero-shot prompting

Zero-shot prompting is when you ask the AI to perform a task it hasn‘t been explicitly trained on, without providing examples. It doesn‘t relate to avoiding specific content.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-a-prompt.html

questions.text: A data science team wants to provide multiple example questions and answers to the model in the prompt so it can better understand the desired format and content of responses. Which prompt engineering technique are they using?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting is a technique where you provide the AI model with a few examples of input-output pairs within the prompt to guide its responses. By including multiple example questions and answers, the model can better understand the desired format, style, and content you expect in its outputs. This method leverages the model‘s ability to recognize patterns and generalize from limited data. It is particularly useful when you want the model to adapt to specific tasks or domains without extensive fine-tuning. In the context of the data science team, supplying several examples helps the model learn how to structure its responses appropriately, improving the relevance and quality of the generated content. Few-shot prompting effectively bridges the gap between zero-shot prompting (no examples) and full fine-tuning (extensive training), offering a practical way to customize the model‘s behavior with minimal effort.

Incorrect

Zero-shot prompting

Zero-shot prompting involves asking the model to perform a task without providing any examples or prior demonstrations. It relies solely on the instructions given in the prompt and does not include example questions and answers.

Single-shot prompting

Single-shot prompting is not a widely recognized term in prompt engineering. If used, it might refer to providing a single example, but it does not involve multiple examples as described in the scenario.

Chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting encourages the model to articulate its reasoning process step-by-step. It focuses on guiding the model through complex reasoning tasks, not on providing multiple examples to illustrate the desired response format.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/jumpstart-foundation-models-customize-prompt-engineering.html

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/few-shot-prompt-engineering-and-fine-tuning-for-llms-in-amazon-bedrock

questions.text: An AI-powered healthcare application you are developing must comply with strict regulations regarding safety, fairness, and inclusivity. Which of the following steps would be most important to ensure the responsible use of AI in this context?

options.text: Implement bias detection tools, conduct human audits, and ensure the use of diverse and curated data sources.
Focus on improving the model's performance without considering external impacts.
Prioritize the speed of deployment to maximize ROI.
Select an AI model that performs best on a public dataset.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Implement bias detection tools, conduct human audits, and ensure the use of diverse and curated data sources.

In the context of AI-powered healthcare, ensuring the responsible use of AI involves addressing fairness, safety, and inclusivity. Bias detection tools help identify and mitigate potential biases in the model, ensuring it does not unfairly impact specific groups. Human audits ensure that the system‘s decision-making is transparent, ethical, and aligns with regulatory standards. Additionally, using diverse and curated data sources helps reduce bias and ensures that the model is inclusive and performs fairly across various populations. These steps are critical in healthcare applications where patient safety and fairness are paramount.

Incorrect

Select an AI model that performs best on a public dataset.

Choosing a model based solely on its performance on public datasets may not guarantee safety, fairness, or inclusivity. Public datasets may contain biases or may not be representative of the real-world data in healthcare settings.

Prioritize the speed of deployment to maximize ROI.

While speed of deployment can be important for business, in healthcare applications, safety, fairness, and regulatory compliance are much more critical than quick deployment.

Focus on improving the model's performance without considering external impacts.

Focusing only on performance without considering fairness, safety, and inclusivity could lead to unintended negative outcomes, particularly in healthcare, where ethical concerns are critical.

questions.text: An online retailer is using a generative AI recommendation engine to suggest products to users. The company wants to measure how often users who interact with the AI end up making purchases. Which metric will best reflect this?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Conversion rate

Conversion rate is the metric that measures the percentage of users who take a desired action, such as making a purchase after interacting with the recommendation engine. For an online retailer, tracking how often users who interact with the AI recommendation system end up making purchases is a direct indicator of the engine's effectiveness. A higher conversion rate would suggest that the AI is successfully driving sales by recommending relevant products.

Incorrect

Efficiency

Efficiency focuses on resource use, such as time or computational power, and does not directly measure user actions like purchases.

Cross-domain performance

Cross-domain performance refers to the AI's ability to work across different areas or tasks, but it is not related to how well the recommendation engine converts interactions into purchases.

Accuracy

Accuracy measures how correct the AI's predictions or recommendations are, but it doesn't directly reflect whether users make purchases after interacting with the AI.

questions.text: A company‘s AI governance policy mandates transparency in the decision-making processes of the AI models. To comply with this, the team must ensure that all data and model decisions are explainable and auditable. What governance protocol is this an example of?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Transparency Standards

Transparency standards in AI governance ensure that the decision-making processes of AI models are explainable, understandable, and auditable. This governance protocol requires the team to provide insights into how AI models make decisions and to ensure that all actions and outcomes are traceable. By adhering to transparency standards, the company can enhance trust, improve accountability, and ensure compliance with regulations that demand explainable AI, especially in sensitive industries like finance or healthcare.

Incorrect

Data Residency

Data residency refers to where data is stored geographically to comply with local laws and regulations. It doesn‘t focus on the explainability or auditability of AI decisions.

Team Training Requirements

Team training requirements ensure that staff are knowledgeable about governance policies, but this does not directly relate to the transparency of AI model decisions.

Review Cadence

Review cadence involves the scheduling of regular evaluations for compliance and governance policies. It does not specifically address transparency in AI decision-making.

questions.text: You are building a machine learning model on Amazon SageMaker, and you want to document the dataset origin, key parameters, and performance metrics to ensure transparency and reproducibility. Which feature of Amazon SageMaker would allow you to document this information?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

SageMaker Model Cards

Amazon SageMaker Model Cards is a feature that allows you to document key details about your machine learning models, including dataset origin, model parameters, and performance metrics. This feature is designed to improve transparency and reproducibility by providing a centralized place to track important information about your models. By using Model Cards, teams can easily share and review the history, performance, and decisions behind each model, making it a useful tool for ensuring compliance, transparency, and accountability in machine learning projects.

Incorrect

SageMaker Ground Truth

SageMaker Ground Truth is a tool for building and managing high-quality training datasets through human labeling. While important for data preparation, it doesn't document model details or performance.

SageMaker Clarify

SageMaker Clarify helps detect bias in data and models and explains model predictions, but it is not used for documenting model parameters or performance metrics.

SageMaker Feature Store

SageMaker Feature Store is a repository for storing and managing machine learning features for reuse, but it does not document the dataset origin or model performance metrics.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-cards.html

questions.text: A financial services company is evaluating generative AI for producing financial reports automatically. They want a model that can adapt to frequent changes in reporting standards and regulations. What is the primary advantage of using generative AI in this scenario?

options.text: Generative AI models are limited by fixed templates and would require full retraining for new data.
Generative AI models have rigid structures and cannot adapt to new data.
Generative AI models are only suitable for creative tasks like generating text or images, not financial reporting.
Generative AI models offer adaptability to new data and regulations with minimal manual updates.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Generative AI models offer adaptability to new data and regulations with minimal manual updates.

Generative AI models are designed to learn patterns and structures from data, allowing them to generate new content based on this learning. In the context of financial reporting, these models can adapt to changes in reporting standards and regulations by being fine-tuned with the latest data and guidelines. This adaptability means that the company can update the model with new information without having to redesign the entire system or perform extensive manual updates. The primary advantage here is the model‘s ability to efficiently incorporate new data and regulatory changes, ensuring that the generated financial reports remain compliant and up-to-date.

Incorrect

Generative AI models have rigid structures and cannot adapt to new data.

Generative AI models are flexible and designed to learn from new data. They can be fine-tuned or retrained with additional datasets to accommodate changes in requirements or data patterns. The assertion that they have rigid structures contradicts the fundamental nature of generative AI, which is built for adaptability and learning.

Generative AI models are limited by fixed templates and would require full retraining for new data.

Generative AI models do not rely on fixed templates; instead, they generate content based on learned patterns from data. While some adjustments may be necessary when incorporating significant changes, they typically do not require full retraining. Fine-tuning with new data is often sufficient to update the model, making it more efficient than systems that depend on static templates.

Generative AI models are only suitable for creative tasks like generating text or images, not financial reporting.

Generating text, including structured documents like financial reports, is well within the capabilities of generative AI models. These models have been successfully used in various industries for tasks that require the generation of coherent and contextually relevant text. Therefore, they are suitable for producing financial reports, which involve generating textual content based on numerical data and regulatory guidelines.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/generative-ai

questions.text: A software development company is looking for an AI model that can help automate parts of the development process by writing code snippets based on user input. Which generative AI use case would best serve this requirement?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Code generation

Code generation involves the use of AI models to automatically produce code snippets, functions, or entire programs based on user input or specifications. For a software development company aiming to automate parts of the development process, this use case is directly relevant. By leveraging machine learning models trained on vast amounts of code, developers can receive real-time code suggestions, complete code fragments, or generate boilerplate code, thereby accelerating development cycles and reducing manual effort. This not only enhances productivity but also helps maintain code quality and consistency across projects. AWS offers services like Amazon Q Developer, which integrates with development environments to provide AI-driven code recommendations.

Incorrect

Audio generation

Audio generation uses AI to create audio content such as music, speech, or sound effects. While it‘s a significant application in entertainment and media industries, it doesn‘t align with the need to generate code snippets for software development.

Summarization

Summarization involves condensing large pieces of text into shorter versions while retaining the main ideas. This is useful for quickly understanding lengthy documents or articles but does not assist in generating code for development purposes.

Translation

Translation uses AI to convert text from one language to another. Although it can be beneficial for translating code comments or documentation, it doesn‘t help in creating new code snippets based on user input.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/q/developer

questions.text: our company is developing an AI system for a car manufacturing plant. The system must recognize different parts on an assembly line using a camera feed. Which AI domain best describes this task?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Computer Vision

Computer Vision (CV) is a field of AI that enables machines to interpret and understand visual data from the world, such as images and videos. It involves techniques like object detection, image classification, and segmentation, allowing systems to analyze and extract meaningful information from visual inputs. In this task, the AI system must recognize different car parts on an assembly line using a camera feed, which directly involves interpreting visual data.

Computer vision specializes in recognizing and understanding objects in images or videos. The system will likely use algorithms like convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to detect and classify various car parts, making CV the most suitable domain to achieve this objective.

Incorrect

Natural Language Processing

Natural Language Processing (NLP) deals with the interaction between computers and human language. It enables machines to understand, interpret, and generate human languages. This domain is more relevant to text or speech data processing, such as language translation or chatbots. Since recognizing car parts from a camera feed involves visual data, NLP is not applicable in this context.

Reinforcement Learning

Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a learning method where an agent interacts with its environment and learns from the feedback it receives. RL is useful in scenarios requiring decision-making based on trial and error, but it is not directly applicable to recognizing objects in images, which is the core task here.

Time-Series Analysis

Time-Series Analysis involves analyzing data points collected or recorded at specific time intervals. It is useful for tasks like forecasting or monitoring temporal patterns, such as stock prices or sensor data. However, recognizing parts on an assembly line from camera footage doesn't involve time-series data.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/computer-vision

questions.text: An AI system designed to predict employee retention shows a significantly different accuracy for predictions based on department. Some departments have much lower prediction accuracy compared to others. Which technique would best help to identify and address this issue?

options.text: Using Amazon Transcribe to improve the training data quality.
Automated hyperparameter tuning to optimize model accuracy.
Real-time model monitoring with Amazon Polly.
Subgroup analysis to evaluate model performance across different departments.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Subgroup analysis to evaluate model performance across different departments.

Subgroup analysis is the best technique to identify and address the issue of varying prediction accuracy across different departments. By analyzing the model's performance for each department separately, the organization can pinpoint if the model is underperforming for specific subgroups. This allows them to identify potential reasons for the discrepancies, such as data imbalances or biases, and take corrective action to improve the model's fairness and accuracy for all departments.

Incorrect

Automated hyperparameter tuning to optimize model accuracy.

Hyperparameter tuning can help improve overall model accuracy, but it doesn't specifically address the performance differences across departments. The issue here is more related to bias or data imbalances rather than the overall model accuracy.

Using Amazon Transcribe to improve the training data quality.

Amazon Transcribe is a service for converting speech to text and is not relevant to improving the quality of training data for an employee retention model, which likely uses structured data.

Real-time model monitoring with Amazon Polly.

Amazon Polly is a service that converts text to speech and is not related to real-time model monitoring or addressing accuracy differences in model predictions across subgroups.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-monitor-data-quality.html

questions.text: A self-driving car company is deploying an AI system to make real-time decisions on the road. They want a model that not only makes safe decisions but is also transparent enough to explain its actions during critical incidents. What is a common tradeoff when prioritizing both safety and transparency in AI models for this type of application?

options.text: The model will achieve both maximum transparency and safety without tradeoffs.
The model will have higher accuracy but may sacrifice transparency entirely.
The model will become less transparent but will increase its decision-making complexity.
The model might achieve high transparency but could suffer from decreased decision-making speed.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

The model might achieve high transparency but could suffer from decreased decision-making speed.

In real-time applications like self-driving cars, there is often a tradeoff between transparency and decision-making speed. Transparent models, such as decision trees or rule-based systems, are easier to explain but can be slower in making decisions compared to more complex, black-box models like deep learning, which are faster but harder to interpret. For critical applications like self-driving cars, ensuring both safety and transparency can lead to slower decisions, especially when the model needs to explain its actions during critical incidents.

Incorrect

The model will have higher accuracy but may sacrifice transparency entirely.

While some black-box models may offer high accuracy, sacrificing transparency entirely is not ideal for self-driving cars, where explainability is important, especially for safety and regulatory reasons.

The model will become less transparent but will increase its decision-making complexity.

Increasing decision-making complexity doesn't necessarily solve the issue of transparency. In fact, more complex models tend to be harder to explain, which is counterproductive in this scenario.

The model will achieve both maximum transparency and safety without tradeoffs.

It is rare to achieve both maximum transparency and safety without some tradeoffs, especially in real-time critical systems. A balance between speed, safety, and explainability is usually required.

questions.text: You are developing a content summarization tool and want to ensure that the entire input text is considered for generating a summary. Which inference parameter should you focus on?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Input length

Input length refers to the amount of text that a model can process at one time. When developing a content summarization tool, ensuring that the entire input text is considered is critical for generating accurate summaries. By focusing on the input length parameter, you can ensure that the model receives and processes the entire text, capturing all relevant information before producing a summary. If the input length is too short, the model may ignore significant parts of the text, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate summaries. Adjusting this parameter allows you to handle longer texts effectively in your summarization application.

Incorrect

Model complexity

Model complexity relates to the number of parameters or layers in the model and impacts the model's ability to handle sophisticated tasks, but it does not control how much input text is considered.

Temperature

Temperature affects the creativity and randomness of the model‘s output but does not determine how much of the input text is considered.

Latency

Latency refers to the time it takes for the model to generate a response, but it doesn't affect how much input text is processed for generating a summary.

questions.text: An AI model that predicts loan approvals performs very well on the training data but fails to generalize well to new applicants from diverse backgrounds. What problem is the model most likely experiencing?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Overfitting

Overfitting occurs when a model learns the patterns in the training data too well, including noise and outliers, making it perform very well on the training data but poorly on new or unseen data. In the case of loan approvals, overfitting means the model is not generalizing well to applicants from diverse backgrounds because it has memorized the training data rather than understanding broader patterns. As a result, the model struggles to handle new applicants that deviate from the characteristics found in the training set. Overfitting is a common problem in machine learning when the model is too complex, has too many features, or has been trained for too many iterations, causing it to be highly sensitive to the training data but unable to adapt to new situations.

Incorrect

Underfitting

Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data. In this case, the model performs poorly on both the training data and new data. Since the model is performing well on training data, underfitting is unlikely.

Low bias and high variance

Low bias and high variance describe an overfitted model. While this option describes overfitting, it‘s not the direct problem. High variance means the model performs inconsistently across different data, but the term overfitting is more precise in this context.

High bias and low variance

High bias means the model is too simplistic and makes incorrect assumptions about the data, leading to underfitting. Low variance suggests the model is stable but inaccurate. This is not the case here, as the model performs well on training data.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/overfitting

questions.text: A company is in the process of evaluating their machine learning model‘s performance using metrics such as accuracy, F1 score, and Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC). Which stage of the ML development lifecycle are they in?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Model evaluation

Model evaluation is the phase of the machine learning lifecycle where the performance of a trained model is assessed using various metrics. Metrics like accuracy, F1 score, and Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) are used to measure how well the model performs on test data. These metrics help determine the model's effectiveness at making correct predictions and identifying patterns. The company is specifically using these metrics to evaluate their model‘s performance, indicating they are in the model evaluation stage. This step is crucial in understanding whether the model is ready for deployment or needs further tuning and improvements.

Incorrect

Model training

Model training involves using a dataset to teach the machine learning algorithm how to recognize patterns in the data. While model evaluation can occur during or after training, model training itself does not involve calculating evaluation metrics like accuracy or AUC.

Data preprocessing

Data preprocessing refers to the preparation of raw data for training, which may involve tasks like cleaning data, handling missing values, or scaling features. It is an earlier phase than model evaluation, and does not involve calculating performance metrics.

Feature selection

Feature selection is the process of selecting the most relevant features from the dataset to improve the model's performance and reduce complexity. This is part of the data preparation phase and comes before model training, so it is not the correct option for evaluating model performance with metrics like F1 score or AUC.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/evaluating_models.html

questions.text: A marketing agency wants to generate personalized product descriptions for different users using a generative AI model. The descriptions must be unique and tailored to user preferences. Which techniques and generative AI model components would be most effective in this scenario? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Few-shot prompt engineering to guide the model's responses
Neural networks with labeled time-series data

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Few-shot prompt engineering to guide the model’s responses

Few-shot prompting provides examples in the prompt to guide the generative AI model toward creating personalized, unique product descriptions tailored to user preferences.

Transformer-based language models with embeddings

Transformer models (like those in Amazon Bedrock) with user preference embeddings enable context-aware generation of customized marketing content.

Incorrect

Real-time inferencing with clustering algorithms

Clustering is unsupervised grouping, not generative; doesn’t create personalized text descriptions.

Supervised learning with classification techniques

Classification predicts categories, not generates unique personalized text content.

Neural networks with labeled time-series data

Time-series for forecasting/sequences, not text generation or personalization.

questions.text: Your team is tasked with optimizing prompt engineering techniques for a chatbot application. One of your goals is to reduce model response variability while maintaining high-quality outputs. Which parameter should you focus on adjusting to achieve this?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Temperature

Temperature controls the randomness of model outputs in generative AI; lower values (e.g., 0.1-0.3) reduce variability for consistent responses while maintaining quality.

Incorrect

Input/output length

Length parameters control token limits but don’t affect response variability or consistency.

Model size

Model size impacts capability and cost, not output randomness during inference.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

questions.text: A company is deciding between fine-tuning a pre-trained model and using in-context learning for its customer support chatbot. What is the primary cost-related tradeoff when choosing fine-tuning over in-context learning?

options.text: Fine-tuning requires significant computational resources and time, but results in a more customized model.
In-context learning requires more time and computational resources but offers a more tailored model.
In-context learning requires expensive hardware upgrades but significantly reduces training time.
Fine-tuning is more expensive initially but offers lower ongoing costs compared to in-context learning.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Fine‑tuning requires significant computational resources and time, but results in a more customized model

  • Correct because fine‑tuning involves retraining a pre‑trained model with domain‑specific data.
  • This process requires compute resources, storage, and time, making it more expensive upfront.
  • The benefit is a highly customized model that performs better for specialized tasks like customer support.
  • The tradeoff is higher initial cost versus improved accuracy and long‑term efficiency.

Incorrect

In‑context learning requires more time and computational resources but offers a more tailored model

  • Incorrect because in‑context learning does not require retraining.
  • It uses examples provided at inference time (via prompts), which is cheaper and faster but less tailored than fine‑tuning.

In‑context learning requires expensive hardware upgrades but significantly reduces training time

  • Incorrect because in‑context learning does not require hardware upgrades.
  • It avoids training altogether, relying on prompt engineering, so this statement is misleading.

Fine‑tuning is more expensive initially but offers lower ongoing costs compared to in‑context learning

  • Incorrect because fine‑tuning does not necessarily reduce ongoing costs.
  • In‑context learning may actually be cheaper long‑term since it avoids retraining and infrastructure costs.

questions.text: A financial institution is trying to use AI to detect fraudulent transactions. They want to identify any unusual patterns in real-time and need to automate their detection processes. Which types of inferencing and AI techniques are best suited for this task? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Real‑time inferencing with deep learning

  • Correct because deep learning models (e.g., neural networks) can capture complex transaction patterns and detect anomalies in real‑time.
  • This is critical for fraud detection, where immediate action is required to block suspicious activity.

Real‑time inferencing with supervised learning

  • Correct because supervised learning models trained on labeled data (fraudulent vs. legitimate transactions) can classify new transactions in real‑time.
  • This enables automated fraud detection pipelines that respond instantly to suspicious behavior.

Incorrect

Real‑time inferencing with unsupervised learning

  • Incorrect because unsupervised learning (e.g., clustering) is useful for anomaly detection but is less effective when labeled fraud data is available.
  • It may generate false positives and is not the primary technique for real‑time fraud detection in financial institutions.

Batch inferencing with supervised learning

  • Incorrect because batch inferencing processes data in bulk, which introduces delays.
  • Fraud detection requires real‑time responses, not delayed batch analysis.

Batch inferencing with clustering algorithms

  • Incorrect because clustering is unsupervised and batch‑based, making it unsuitable for real‑time fraud detection.
  • It may help in exploratory analysis but not in immediate fraud prevention.

questions.text: A company is building a model to predict housing prices based on historical sales data. They collect a dataset containing house size, location, and the year built. The model will use this data to estimate future house prices. Which of the following best describes this type of learning?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct Supervised learning

  • Correct because supervised learning uses labeled datasets (input features + known output).
  • In this case, the dataset includes features (house size, location, year built) and the label (historical house price).
  • The model learns the relationship between inputs and outputs to predict future prices.
  • This is a classic regression problem under supervised learning.

Incorrect Unstructured learning

  • Incorrect because “unstructured learning” is not a standard machine learning category.
  • The dataset here is structured (tabular data with defined features and labels).

Unsupervised learning

  • Incorrect because unsupervised learning deals with unlabeled data (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction).
  • In this scenario, the dataset has labels (house prices), so it is not unsupervised.

Reinforcement learning

  • Incorrect because reinforcement learning involves agents learning through trial and error with rewards and penalties.
  • Predicting housing prices does not involve an agent interacting with an environment or receiving rewards.

questions.text: Your organization is building an AI system that processes highly sensitive financial data. You are tasked with ensuring that the data remains secure during transmission across AWS. Which AWS feature or service would best help you secure the data in transit?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

AWS PrivateLink

  • Correct because AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs, AWS services, and on‑premises applications without exposing traffic to the public internet.
  • This ensures that sensitive financial data remains secure during transmission, meeting the requirement of protecting data in transit.
  • It is specifically designed for secure communication, reducing risks of interception or accidental exposure.

Incorrect

Amazon CloudFront

  • Incorrect because CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) used for caching and distributing content globally.
  • While it supports HTTPS for secure delivery, it is not the best solution for securing sensitive financial data in transit between internal systems.

AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

  • Incorrect because IAM manages authentication and authorization (who can access what).
  • It does not secure data during transmission; instead, it controls access permissions.

Amazon Macie

  • Incorrect because Macie is a data security and privacy service that uses ML to discover and classify sensitive data in S3.
  • It helps with compliance and data classification but does not secure data in transit.

questions.text: While working on a text generation task, you want the model to explain its reasoning process step-by-step. Which prompt engineering technique would be the most effective for achieving this?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting is a technique where you instruct the AI model to articulate its reasoning process in a step-by-step manner. By including prompts like “explain each step“ or “let‘s think through this together,“ you encourage the model to break down its thought process as it arrives at an answer. This method is particularly effective when you want transparency in how the model reaches conclusions, especially for complex tasks like problem-solving or decision-making. By guiding the model to outline its reasoning, you not only get the final output but also the logical steps that led to it. This can help in verifying the accuracy of the response and provides insights into the model‘s understanding of the task. Chain-of-thought prompting enhances the quality of the generated text by ensuring that each step logically follows the previous one, resulting in a coherent and comprehensive explanation.

Incorrect

Zero-shot prompting

Zero-shot prompting involves asking the model to perform a task it hasn‘t been explicitly trained on, without providing examples. It doesn‘t specifically guide the model to explain its reasoning step-by-step.

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting provides the model with a few examples within the prompt to help it understand the desired output. While it can guide style and format, it doesn‘t inherently encourage step-by-step reasoning.

Negative prompting

Negative prompting instructs the model on what to avoid in its response. It focuses on prohibiting certain content rather than encouraging the model to elaborate on its reasoning process.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/what-is-prompt-engineering.html

questions.text: A development team is assessing the performance of their foundation model by having a group of users rate the accuracy and relevance of the model's outputs. What is this evaluation approach called?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Human evaluation

Human evaluation is a process where human users assess the performance of a model by rating the accuracy, relevance, and quality of its outputs. In the context of foundation models, this method allows the development team to gather subjective feedback directly from people who interact with the model. Human evaluation is especially useful in scenarios where the model‘s performance is difficult to measure using traditional metrics, as it helps to capture the nuances of user satisfaction and the relevance of the model‘s responses. This approach ensures that the model‘s outputs align with human preferences and real-world expectations.

Incorrect

Benchmark testing

Benchmark testing involves comparing the model‘s performance against a set of predefined metrics or standard datasets, not user-generated ratings of the model‘s outputs.

Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning is the process of adjusting a pre-trained model to better fit a specific task or dataset. It does not refer to the act of having users evaluate the model‘s outputs.

Zero-shot learning

Zero-shot learning refers to a model‘s ability to handle tasks it hasn‘t been explicitly trained on. This is unrelated to the process of users evaluating the model‘s performance.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/clarify-foundation-model-evaluate-human.html

questions.text: A company wants to improve the quality of AI-generated text by adjusting how the input prompt is provided to a transformer-based large language model (LLM). What is the term for designing effective input prompts to maximize the accuracy and relevance of the model‘s output?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Prompt engineering

Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and optimizing input prompts to elicit the most accurate and relevant responses from a language model. In the context of transformer-based large language models (LLMs), the quality of the generated text heavily depends on how the input prompt is structured. By carefully crafting prompts, developers can guide the model to produce outputs that better align with the desired outcome. This involves selecting the right words, phrases, and formats to provide clear instructions or context to the model. Effective prompt engineering can significantly enhance the model‘s performance without altering its underlying architecture or retraining it. It is a cost-effective way to improve AI-generated text quality, making it more coherent, contextually appropriate, and useful for applications like customer service chatbots, virtual assistants, and content generation tools.

Incorrect

Tokenization

Tokenization is the process of breaking down text into smaller units called tokens, such as words, subwords, or characters. While tokenization is essential for preparing text data for processing by LLMs, it does not involve designing or adjusting input prompts to improve output quality. Tokenization focuses on text preprocessing rather than optimizing prompt design.

Model training

Model training refers to the process of teaching a machine learning model to perform a specific task by exposing it to data and adjusting its internal parameters. Although training can improve a model‘s performance, it is a resource-intensive process and does not address the immediate need to enhance output quality by adjusting input prompts. The question focuses on improving responses through prompt design, not through retraining the model.

Embedding optimization

Embedding optimization involves refining the vector representations of words or tokens to improve how a model understands semantic relationships in language. While embeddings are crucial for a model‘s internal comprehension, optimizing them is a complex process that does not pertain to adjusting the input prompts provided to the model. Embedding optimization deals with the model‘s internal workings rather than the external design of prompts.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/prompt-engineering

questions.text: You are developing a foundation model for medical applications and want to ensure that the model is not biased against certain demographic groups. Which AWS service can help detect and mitigate bias in the training data?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon SageMaker Clarify

Amazon SageMaker Clarify helps detect and mitigate bias in machine learning models and datasets. It provides tools for monitoring models to ensure fairness and transparency by identifying potential biases in the data during the training process. SageMaker Clarify helps generate insights about the data and the model's behavior across different demographic groups, ensuring that sensitive applications, such as medical models, do not inadvertently discriminate against any group. This makes it a crucial service for building ethical and unbiased AI models, particularly in sensitive domains like healthcare.

Incorrect

Amazon Rekognition

Amazon Rekognition is a computer vision service that helps analyze images and videos. It does not provide tools for detecting or mitigating bias in machine learning models or datasets.

AWS Macie

AWS Macie is a service for identifying and protecting sensitive information like personally identifiable information (PII). While important for data security, it does not address bias detection or mitigation.

Amazon Textract

Amazon Textract extracts text and data from documents but does not offer features for detecting or mitigating bias in training data or machine learning models.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/clarify

questions.text: A retail business wants to improve product recommendations for customers by analyzing past purchase behavior. Which type of AI/ML solution would most likely provide value for this use case?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Recommendation System

A recommendation system is the most suitable AI/ML solution for a retail business looking to improve product recommendations based on past purchase behavior. Recommendation systems analyze customer behavior, such as purchase history, browsing patterns, and product ratings, to suggest relevant items that users might be interested in. These systems often employ collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, or a hybrid approach to make personalized suggestions. In retail, recommendation systems enhance the customer experience by providing tailored product recommendations, which can increase engagement and sales. Popular e-commerce platforms like Amazon, Netflix, and Spotify use recommendation systems to offer personalized suggestions based on user preferences. AWS offers tools like Amazon Personalize, which provides pre-built algorithms specifically designed to create personalized recommendations, making it easier for businesses to implement and deploy recommendation systems.

Incorrect

Regression

Regression models are used to predict continuous values, such as sales revenue or customer spending, based on historical data. While useful for predicting numerical outcomes, regression is not specifically designed for making personalized product recommendations.

Clustering

Clustering involves grouping similar data points together based on their features. While clustering can help segment customers into different groups, but it does not provide the same level of personalization as a recommendation system for suggesting products.

Classification

Classification algorithms are used to categorize data into distinct classes or labels, such as fraud detection or spam filtering. While valuable for specific predictive tasks, classification is not designed for recommending products based on customer behavior.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/personalize/latest/dg/what-is-personalize.html

questions.text: A mobile application requires text-to-speech functionality to enhance accessibility by reading on-screen text aloud for visually impaired users. Which AWS service can provide this capability?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Polly

Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech using advanced deep learning models, offering a variety of voices and languages. This service is highly useful for creating applications that cater to visually impaired users or those with reading difficulties. It can read content such as documents, notifications, or web pages in real-time, making the application more accessible. Polly‘s API is easy to integrate into mobile and web applications, and it supports multiple speech formats, including MP3, OGG, and PCM. Additionally, Amazon Polly offers customization features, such as adjusting the speaking rate, pitch, and pronunciation, ensuring a better user experience.

Incorrect

Amazon Translate

Amazon Translate is a machine translation service that automatically converts text from one language to another. While it is valuable for multilingual applications, it does not provide text-to-speech functionality.

Amazon Lex

Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces like chatbots and voice-based applications. While it integrates speech recognition and text-to-speech for chatbots, its primary focus is on conversation flow rather than standalone text-to-speech features needed for accessibility.

Amazon SageMaker

Amazon SageMaker is a platform for building, training, and deploying machine learning models. It is not specifically designed for text-to-speech functionality, and using it for this purpose would require significant customization and development effort.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/polly

questions.text: You are designing an AI application that involves multiple steps, such as gathering customer data, processing it, and then providing personalized recommendations. Which of the following is a key advantage of using agents to manage this multi-step task?

options.text: Agents can autonomously orchestrate and manage each step of the task, adapting dynamically as needed.
Agents minimize the amount of human input required by fully automating all steps.
Agents decrease model complexity by eliminating the need for sequential task execution.
Agents handle only the initial data gathering phase, requiring manual intervention for the rest.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Agents can autonomously orchestrate and manage each step of the task, adapting dynamically as needed.

A key advantage of using agents in an AI application with multiple steps is that they can autonomously manage and orchestrate each part of the task. Agents can execute actions in a sequence or adapt their behavior dynamically based on the data they receive and process. This adaptability allows for a more streamlined and efficient workflow, reducing the need for manual intervention. Agents are ideal for managing complex, multi-step processes like gathering customer data, processing it, and providing personalized recommendations in an automated fashion.

Incorrect

Agents minimize the amount of human input required by fully automating all steps.

While agents reduce the need for human input, they may not fully automate all steps, as certain tasks might still require human oversight or decision-making.

Agents handle only the initial data gathering phase, requiring manual intervention for the rest.

Agents can manage the entire process, not just the initial data-gathering phase. They are designed to handle multiple steps autonomously.

Agents decrease model complexity by eliminating the need for sequential task execution

Agents do not eliminate the need for sequential task execution. Instead, they manage complex tasks, often executing them sequentially when needed, while maintaining adaptability and efficiency.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents.html

questions.text: During an AI assessment, you notice that certain prompts cause the model to generate biased or harmful content. This issue arises from malicious data injected during training. What is this type of risk called?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Model poisoning

Model poisoning is a type of adversarial attack where malicious actors inject harmful or biased data into the training dataset of an AI model. This corrupted data influences the learning process, causing the model to develop unintended behaviors or generate biased and harmful content when given certain prompts. The injected data can be designed to exploit vulnerabilities in the model, leading it to produce outputs that are misleading, offensive, or even dangerous. Model poisoning is particularly concerning because it compromises the model from the inside, making it difficult to detect through regular evaluation methods. This risk emphasizes the importance of securing the training pipeline, implementing strict data validation procedures, and continuously monitoring the model‘s outputs for anomalies. By protecting against model poisoning, developers can ensure the integrity and reliability of AI systems, safeguarding them from malicious influences that could undermine their functionality and trustworthiness.

Incorrect

Exposure

Exposure refers to the risk of an AI model unintentionally revealing sensitive or confidential information it was trained on. While it‘s a significant concern, it doesn‘t involve malicious data injection during training.

Prompt hijacking

Prompt hijacking involves manipulating the input prompts to trick the AI into producing unintended or undesirable outputs. It targets the model at inference time, not through the training data.

Instruction tuning

Instruction tuning is a method of fine-tuning AI models using datasets that include explicit instructions and responses. It is a training technique aimed at improving performance, not a risk associated with malicious data.

questions.text: A startup wants to develop a generative AI model to provide real-time text generation services. However, the team is small, and they lack extensive machine learning expertise. How can AWS generative AI services lower the barrier to entry for this team?

options.text: By offering fully managed services with pre-trained models and no need for machine learning expertise.
By providing pre-built infrastructure for deploying applications in multiple regions.
By offering full control over on-premises deployments for the AI models.
By reducing costs through long-term usage contracts.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

By offering fully managed services with pre-trained models and no need for machine learning expertise.

AWS generative AI services, such as Amazon Bedrock, provide pre-trained models that can be easily fine-tuned for specific use cases without requiring deep machine learning expertise. These services offer fully managed infrastructure, allowing developers to focus on their application rather than the complexities of building and training models from scratch. This significantly low0ers the barrier to entry for small teams or startups, making it easier to deploy generative AI solutions.

Incorrect

By providing pre-built infrastructure for deploying applications in multiple regions.

While AWS offers infrastructure to deploy applications globally, this feature does not specifically address the need for simplifying generative AI model development.

By reducing costs through long-term usage contracts.

Reducing costs through long-term contracts is related to pricing strategy but does not directly help with the challenges of developing or managing generative AI models for teams lacking expertise.

By offering full control over on-premises deployments for the AI models.

AWS focuses on cloud-based solutions, and offering control over on-premises deployments does not directly lower the barrier to entry for teams looking to use managed services for generative AI.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock

questions.text: You are developing an AI-driven loan approval system. Your team is concerned that the model could unintentionally favor applicants from certain regions based on historical loan data. Which responsible AI principle should you consider addressing to ensure fairness in the loan approval process?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Bias

Bias in AI refers to systematic errors or prejudices in data or algorithms that lead to unfair outcomes, often favoring one group over others. In the context of your AI-driven loan approval system, the concern is that the model could unintentionally favor applicants from certain regions due to biases present in historical loan data. This means the AI might grant loans more readily to individuals from certain areas while disadvantaging others, perpetuating existing inequalities. Addressing bias involves identifying and mitigating these unfair tendencies in both your data and algorithms. Techniques to reduce bias include rebalancing your dataset to ensure all regions are adequately represented, removing or anonymizing location data if it‘s not relevant to creditworthiness, and applying fairness constraints during model training. By focusing on bias, you aim to create a fair loan approval process that assesses applicants based on relevant financial criteria rather than irrelevant regional factors, ensuring equitable treatment for all applicants.

Incorrect

Veracity

Veracity relates to the accuracy and reliability of data. While ensuring data correctness is important, it doesn‘t directly address the issue of the model favoring applicants from certain regions due to historical biases.

Inclusivity

Inclusivity focuses on designing AI systems that are accessible and effective for a diverse range of users. While it promotes broad accessibility, it doesn‘t specifically tackle the problem of biased decision-making based on regional data.

Robustness

Robustness refers to an AI system‘s ability to perform reliably under various conditions and resist errors or adversarial inputs. It doesn‘t address fairness or the elimination of biases related to favoring certain regions.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/ai/responsible-ai

questions.text: Your team has been tasked with building a generative AI application that can produce high-quality text summaries from customer feedback. You are considering various AWS services to help accelerate development and deployment. Which AWS service offers a curated collection of pre-built models and solutions to simplify the development of generative AI applications?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

Amazon SageMaker JumpStart offers a curated collection of pre-built machine learning models and solutions, making it easier to develop and deploy machine learning and generative AI applications. It provides access to pre-trained models from various domains, including natural language processing (NLP), which can be helpful for tasks like summarizing customer feedback. Developers can quickly fine-tune these models with their data and deploy them, significantly accelerating the development process without needing to build models from scratch.

Incorrect

Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler

Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler simplifies the process of data preparation by offering tools to clean, explore, and transform data. While essential for data management, it does not provide pre-built models for generative AI.

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a repository designed to store and manage features for machine learning models. It helps ensure consistency between training and inference, but it is not focused on pre-built models or generative AI tasks.

Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor

Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor helps detect data quality issues in machine learning models in real-time. It ensures model performance remains consistent, but it does not offer pre-built models or simplify the development of generative AI applications.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/jumpstart

questions.text: You are tasked with improving a company‘s knowledge base by integrating AI to allow users to ask complex questions and receive detailed, contextually relevant answers from the company‘s internal documents. What AWS service can you leverage to implement Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) in this system?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon Bedrock

Amazon Bedrock allows organizations to build, scale, and deploy powerful AI models for various use cases, including Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). Bedrock provides access to pre-trained foundation models from multiple providers, allowing you to create systems that combine retrieval and natural language generation capabilities. By using Bedrock, you can integrate large language models with retrieval capabilities to answer complex questions by fetching relevant information from internal documents. This service is ideal for companies looking to enhance their knowledge bases with RAG, as it simplifies the deployment of AI models that can provide contextual and detailed responses.

Incorrect

Amazon Rekognition

Amazon Rekognition is a service used for image and video analysis, such as object detection and facial recognition. It is not designed for text-based information retrieval or natural language generation.

Amazon Polly

Amazon Polly is a service that converts text into lifelike speech. While useful for text-to-speech applications, it does not support complex question answering or document retrieval.

AWS Glue

AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service that helps prepare and move data for analytics. It is unrelated to AI-powered question-answering systems or the implementation of RAG.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/knowledge-bases

questions.text: What is natural language processing (NLP)?

options.text: A method for training models with large, unlabeled datasets.
A machine learning task is used to predict future values in a dataset.
A field of AI focused on enabling machines to understand and generate human language.
A type of deep learning used for image classification.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

A field of AI focused on enabling machines to understand and generate human language.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a subfield of artificial intelligence (AI) that focuses on enabling machines to understand, interpret, and generate human language in a meaningful way. NLP encompasses a range of tasks such as text analysis, speech recognition, sentiment analysis, translation, and more. The goal of NLP is to bridge the gap between human communication and machine understanding by processing language in ways that enable computers to perform tasks like summarizing text, extracting key phrases, or responding to human queries.

Incorrect

A machine learning task is used to predict future values in a dataset.

This describes time series forecasting, which is not specific to NLP.

A type of deep learning used for image classification

This describes convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are commonly used for image classification tasks, but it is unrelated to NLP.

A method for training models with large, unlabeled datasets

This describes unsupervised learning or self-supervised learning, which may be used in NLP but is not exclusive to it.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/nlp

questions.text: A company uses an AI model to predict product demand, but training and maintaining the model has become expensive. They want to evaluate the financial viability of continuing the project. Which business metric would provide the best insight?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Cost per user

Cost per user is the best business metric for evaluating the financial viability of continuing a project, especially when costs are a concern. This metric measures how much it costs the company to train, maintain, and run the AI model per user or prediction. By understanding the costs involved in delivering the predictions, the company can determine whether the expense of maintaining the AI model is justified relative to the value it provides. If the costs are too high compared to the benefits or revenue generated, the company can decide whether to optimize the model, reduce costs, or discontinue the project.

Incorrect

Accuracy

Accuracy measures how well the model performs in terms of making correct predictions. While important for evaluating model performance, it does not directly provide insight into the financial viability of the project.

Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC)

AUC evaluates the model's ability to distinguish between classes, particularly for classification problems. While it reflects model performance, it does not provide information about the financial costs or viability of the project.

Precision

Precision measures how many of the predicted positive outcomes are actually correct. Like accuracy and AUC, it is a model performance metric, not a business metric focused on financial viability.

questions.text: You are tasked with building an AI application that requires the storage and querying of large volumes of text data for real-time analysis. Which AWS service would best handle full-text search and analytics for this use case?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon OpenSearch Service

Amazon OpenSearch Service is a fully managed service that enables you to search, analyze, and visualize large volumes of data in real time. It is optimized for full-text search and can handle large datasets with low-latency querying, making it ideal for applications that require quick and efficient text search and analysis. OpenSearch also supports advanced analytics, including visualizations, and integrates well with other AWS services. This makes it an excellent choice for AI applications that need to store and query large amounts of text data in real time.

Incorrect

Amazon RDS

Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service. While suitable for structured data, it is not optimized for full-text search and real-time text analytics like OpenSearch.

AWS Glue

AWS Glue is a data integration service designed for ETL processes. It is not intended for full-text search and analytics but is used for preparing data for analytics and machine learning.

Amazon Comprehend

Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing (NLP) service that helps extract insights from text, such as sentiment analysis or key phrases. However, it is not a solution for storing and querying large volumes of text data for real-time search.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service

questions.text: A team is working with a pre-trained language model and wants to adapt it for legal document generation. They plan to provide task-specific instructions to fine-tune the model. What fine-tuning method are they using?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Instruction tuning

Instruction tuning is a fine-tuning method where a pre-trained model is given task-specific instructions to adjust its performance for a particular task.
